# Running your own package server

This page is for developers, agencies and hosts who want installations to download site packages from a server of
their own: for packages that are not public yet, for a set tested for one customer, or as a mirror. Nothing on a
package server runs code; it is a folder of files served over HTTPS.

7x and the Exponential Foundation strongly encourage you to also submit your site package by pull request to
se7enxweb/exponential.packages.exponential.earth, the server every installation reads by default: see
[Contribute your site package](../contribute-your-site-package.md).

## What a server must answer

The clients read one file, `<index URL>/index.xml`, and then each archive at the `url` the index gives:

| Client | Reads | Code |
|---|---|---|
| setup wizard, kickstarter, `exp:install` | `package.ini [RepositorySettings] RemotePackagesIndexURL` + `/index.xml` | `kernel/setup/steps/ezstep_site_types.php` |
| ezupdate (**Package servers**, `fetch`) | the server's URL + `/index.xml` | `extension/ezupdate/classes/ezupdatepackageservers.php` |

The 7x server answers at `https://exponential.packages.exponential.earth/exponential/6.0/6.0.15/index.xml`. More on
[What the package server is](../package-server/what-the-package-server-is.md).

## The folder layout

Mirror the 7x layout, so `RemotePackagesIndexURLBase` works for your server too (the kernel appends
`/<major.minor>/<version>` when `RemotePackagesIndexURL` is empty):

```text
https://packages.example.com/exponential/
└── 6.0/
    └── 6.0.15/
        ├── index.xml
        ├── acme_site.ezpkg
        ├── acme_site_democontent.ezpkg
        └── thumbnails/
            └── acme_site.png
```

One folder per Exponential release keeps old installations working: an installation of 6.0.14 keeps reading its
folder while you publish for the next release.

## A complete index.xml

```xml
<?xml version="1.0"?>
<packages vendor="acme">
  <package name="acme_site_democontent" type="contentobject"
           url="https://packages.example.com/exponential/6.0/6.0.15/acme_site_democontent.ezpkg"/>
  <package name="sevenx_classes" type="contentclass"
           url="https://exponential.packages.exponential.earth/exponential/6.0/6.0.15/sevenx_classes.ezpkg"/>
  <package name="acme_site" version="1.0.0-1" type="site"
           summary="Acme starter site"
           description="What an editor gets after installing it."
           url="https://packages.example.com/exponential/6.0/6.0.15/acme_site.ezpkg"
           thumbnail_url="https://packages.example.com/exponential/6.0/6.0.15/thumbnails/acme_site.png"/>
</packages>
```

- The root element must be `<packages>`; the wizard reports "Malformed index file." otherwise.
- Every `<package>` needs `name` and `url`; site packages also `type="site"` (the wizard lists only those), a
  `summary`, a `version` and a `thumbnail_url`. The 7x index uses the same attributes.
- **Every package a site package requires must be in the same index.** The wizard looks a required package up in the
  index it read, not on other servers. Its `url` may point anywhere, including the 7x server, as `sevenx_classes`
  does above.

The format in full: [The index.xml format](../package-server/the-index-xml-format.md).

## Hosting on GitHub Pages

The 7x server is the repository
[se7enxweb/exponential.packages.exponential.earth](https://github.com/se7enxweb/exponential.packages.exponential.earth)
published by GitHub Pages:

| File | Role |
|---|---|
| `exponential/6.0/<version>/` | the release folders |
| `CNAME` | the custom domain the Pages site answers on |
| `.github/workflows/workflow.yml` | on every push: checks out the branch `master`, generates directory listings with `jayanta525/github-pages-directory-listing`, uploads the tree and deploys it with `actions/deploy-pages`; one deployment at a time (`concurrency: pages`) |

To do the same: create a repository, add the folders and a copy of the workflow (change `ref:` to your default
branch), enable GitHub Pages for the repository, and optionally add a `CNAME` with your domain.
Details on [The package server on GitHub](../package-server/the-package-server-on-github.md).

> **Note**
> Each deployment publishes the whole tree as of its commit, and, as `settings/package.ini` puts it, "a package server
> that is being republished answers with errors for a few minutes". The setup wizard retries for that reason (`DownloadAttempts`, `DownloadRetryDelays[]`); see
> [When the package server cannot be reached](../package-server/when-the-package-server-cannot-be-reached.md).

## Hosting on any web server

Any server that serves static files over HTTPS works:

```bash
rsync -av exponential/ deploy@packages.example.com:/srv/packages/exponential/
curl -sI https://packages.example.com/exponential/6.0/6.0.15/index.xml | head -1
```

Serve the folder read-only, with no scripts, and keep the files in git so every published state can be traced.

## Limits and checks of the clients

| Check | Setup wizard | ezupdate |
|---|---|---|
| Scheme | any URL PHP can fetch | `https://` only, also for redirects |
| HTTP status | an answer other than 200 fails the attempt | an error status fails |
| Archive | must start with the gzip signature, must not be empty or shorter than announced | at most 256 MiB |
| Index | parsed as XML, root `<packages>` | at most 1 MiB, root `<packages>` |
| Retries | `DownloadAttempts` (3) with `DownloadRetryDelays[]` (2, 5, 10 s) | none |
| Timeouts | `DownloadTimeout` 300 s, `DownloadConnectTimeout` 30 s | 300 s, connect 15 s |

Use HTTPS for every URL in your index so both clients accept it.

## Checklist

- [ ] `curl -sI` on `index.xml`, each archive and each thumbnail answers `200`.
- [ ] `xmllint --noout index.xml` passes.
- [ ] Each archive passes `php ezpm.php validate` ([Rebuilding with build.sh](rebuilding-with-build-sh.md)).
- [ ] Every `<require>` of every site package has an entry in the index.
- [ ] Index `version` values equal the archives' `<number>-<release>`.
- [ ] A dry run against the server succeeds ([Testing in a sandbox](testing-in-a-sandbox.md)).
